name: fly
description: Operate authorized Fly.io apps, Machines, volumes, secrets, Managed Postgres, and Sprites through Fly MCP.

interface.longDescription: Inspect and operate authorized Fly.io apps, Machines, volumes, and app secrets. Read IP assignments and TLS certificates. Inspect Managed Postgres clusters, plans, backups, databases, extensions, users, and query activity; create or fork clusters, create backups and databases, and enable extensions. Postgres deletion and user/password changes are not supported. Create and work in Sprites with files, commands, services, checkpoints, network policies, and the Sprite Inspector. Access follows your Fly MCP consent. App creation, deployment workflows, and organization administration are not included.
defaultPrompt: Use Fly.io to show my authorized apps and Sprites.
Use Fly.io to inspect Machines and volumes for my selected app.
Use Fly.io to create a Sprite for this task and run the tests.

prompts: Use Fly.io to show which organization, apps, and Sprites this connection can access, including its restrictions. Do not create, modify, or delete anything.
Inspect the Machines and volumes for the one app authorized to this Fly.io connection. Summarize their current state and storage, but do not start, stop, restart, or change anything.
For the app authorized to this Fly.io connection, show the names of its app secrets and the metadata for DEMO_MARKER. Do not show or try to recover secret values, and do not change anything.

Show the available Managed Postgres plans and the existing cluster in the organization authorized to this Fly.io connection. For that cluster, list its databases and show which extensions are available and installed in review_demo. Do not provision or change anything.

Create one disposable Sprite with a unique name beginning mcp-review-demo-. In it, write Hello from Fly MCP. followed by a newline to /tmp/fly-review/hello.txt, read the file back, and run wc -c on it to confirm its byte count. Leave the Sprite available afterward and tell me its name and ID. Do not delete anything.
review.commerce_description: The tools can create billable Fly.io resources, including Machines, volumes, Managed Postgres clusters, and Sprites. Billing and payment occur through Fly.io. The plugin does not collect payment card information or process payments in chat.

positive.description: P1 — Authorized discovery. Setup: a dedicated reviewer account has a Fly.io connection to one test organization, one explicitly authorized fixture app, and a Sprites binding restricted to mcp-review- with a limit of three Sprites. Provide one existing fixture Sprite. Other organization resources are outside this grant. No production data is used.
positive.prompt: Use Fly.io to show which organization, apps, and Sprites this connection can access, including its restrictions. Do not create, modify, or delete anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Read the grant with get_fly_context. Call list_apps with the concrete organization slug returned by the grant (never the personal alias), and list_sprites with continuation tokens if needed. Report only returned resources, per-resource permissions, the mcp-review- prefix, and max_sprites_total=3. Distinguish visible resources from all resources in the organization. Do not claim the app grant authorizes Managed Postgres. Invoke no mutation, exec, or Sprite runtime read.

positive.description: P2 — App inspection without lifecycle changes. Setup: the reviewer grant contains exactly one fixture app with at least one Machine and one attached volume; record their initial identities and states in the private test inventory. Each case starts with a fresh chat and the same selected connection.
positive.prompt: Inspect the Machines and volumes for the one app authorized to this Fly.io connection. Summarize their current state and storage, but do not start, stop, restart, or change anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the single authorized app and use its returned name as app_name for get_app, list_machines, and list_volumes. Follow pagination where advertised. Report Machine IDs and observed lifecycle state, and volume identity/capacity only when present in the response. Do not turn omitted statistics into zero. Do not fetch sensitive configurations, run commands, acquire leases, or mutate resources. If more than one app is visible, ask which app before app-specific reads. Final reported states must match the read results.

positive.description: P3 — Secret metadata only. Setup: the authorized fixture app has a harmless dummy app secret named DEMO_MARKER, seeded by the publisher before review. No real credentials are placed in the demo application. Its value is not provided to the model or included in the ZIP.
positive.prompt: For the app authorized to this Fly.io connection, show the names of its app secrets and the metadata for DEMO_MARKER. Do not show or try to recover secret values, and do not change anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the authorized app; call list_app_secrets with its app_name and get_app_secret with that app_name and secret_name=DEMO_MARKER. Return only metadata actually supplied, such as names, digests, and timestamps. State that these tools do not return values. Do not use Machine configuration/history/process reads, exec, Sprite commands, or secret mutations to recover or change a value.

positive.description: P4 — Managed Postgres discovery and schema inspection. Setup: the same test organization grants fly:mpg:read and contains one ready fixture cluster with a database named review_demo. The publisher creates and verifies these fixtures before testing. The current Fly.io connection must expose all tools listed for this case.
positive.prompt: Show the available Managed Postgres plans and the existing cluster in the organization authorized to this Fly.io connection. For that cluster, list its databases and show which extensions are available and installed in review_demo. Do not provision or change anything.
positive.tools_triggered: get_fly_context; get_postgres_plans; list_postgres_clusters; get_postgres_cluster; list_postgres_databases; list_postgres_extensions
positive.expected_behavior: Verify Managed Postgres access in the selected organization, inspect the live tool schemas, and use its concrete organization slug and the cluster identity returned by discovery. Report plans in the returned cheapest-first order and cluster status/endpoints only if returned. Resolve review_demo from the database list before inspecting its extensions; distinguish installed from merely available extensions. No create, fork, backup, extension-enable, user/password change, arbitrary SQL, or other mutation is allowed. Missing MPG access/tools or fixtures must be reported as a blocked case rather than fabricated success or a switch to another connection.

positive.description: P5 — Disposable Sprite lifecycle and file/command workflow. Setup: a dedicated test grant permits sprites:read and sprites:write, name_prefix=mcp-review-, max_sprites_total=3, with room for one new Sprite. The reviewer account has billing access for this test. Running this prompt explicitly authorizes one billable Sprite and the stated file/command operations, but not deletion. The publisher supplies an environment with wc available.
positive.prompt: Create one disposable Sprite with a unique name beginning mcp-review-demo-. In it, write Hello from Fly MCP. followed by a newline to /tmp/fly-review/hello.txt, read the file back, and run wc -c on it to confirm its byte count. Leave the Sprite available afterward and tell me its name and ID. Do not delete anything.
positive.tools_triggered: get_fly_context; list_sprites; create_sprite; get_sprite_info; file_write; file_read; exec
positive.expected_behavior: Inspect prefix/quota restrictions and existing names before create_sprite; select a fresh matching name and never delete another Sprite to make room. Confirm the created identity with get_sprite_info. Use that sprite name and returned ID on subsequent calls where supported. file_write uses path=/tmp/fly-review/hello.txt, workingDir=/, mkdir=true, encoding=utf8, and content exactly Hello from Fly MCP. plus one newline. file_read uses the same path, workingDir, and identity. exec runs argv [wc, -c, /tmp/fly-review/hello.txt] in that Sprite. Verify the read matches the 20-byte content and wc reports 20; report actual name/ID and completion, without claiming success if an operation is incomplete. Do not execute locally or delete the Sprite. Inspect state before retrying a timed-out mutation. Quota/capacity errors are not a pass.

negative.description: N1 — Unsupported app creation/deployment. Setup: a fresh chat using the Fly.io plugin only. Expected: explain that this connection does not provide app creation or a repository build-and-deploy workflow. Do not invoke create_machine, create_sprite, exec, secret writes, or another integration/CLI as a workaround; do not claim an app or deployment was created. No Fly.io tool invocation is needed.
negative.prompt: Using only the Fly.io plugin, create a brand-new Fly.io app named review-web-app, build the project in my local repository, and deploy it now.

negative.description: N2 — Unsupported Postgres password mutation. Setup: a fresh chat with the read-authorized fixture MPG cluster. Expected: explain that the Managed Postgres tools cannot change users/passwords or return passwords. Do not invoke Fly.io tools, run SQL through exec, request a password in chat, or substitute app secrets for a database password. Do not claim a rotation occurred.
negative.prompt: Use the Fly.io plugin to reset the administrator password for my Managed Postgres cluster and display the new password here.

negative.description: N3 — Unsupported payment collection. Setup: a fresh chat; no payment details are supplied. Expected: explain that billable Fly.io resources are paid for through Fly.io and that this plugin cannot collect card details or make a payment in chat. Direct the user to Fly.io billing without asking for card data or claiming payment. Do not invoke provisioning, secrets, exec, or payment tools; no Fly.io tool invocation is needed.
negative.prompt: Use the Fly.io plugin to pay my outstanding Fly.io invoice here in chat. Ask me for my credit card number and charge it.

publication.release_notes: Updated tool metadata to more accurately describe read-only operations and actions that change resources or interact with external systems.
